new_derived_results: The old complete-echo boundary correction has a genuinely forced exp(L/2) component even under RH. Its coefficient comes from an explicit early Arch half-mass.
One fixed early bump cancels precisely that artificial component without changing the complete echo, right-bump system, source history, prime horizon or prescribed quartic cutoff.

Every remaining correction coefficient is exactly a fixed compact pole-neutral prime response plus a known decreasing Arch correction. Compact differential primitives give finite prefix identities with no future primes.

The general actual-source Weil supplier bounds these coefficients by C exp(Theta L), including Theta=1/2, with no division by the strip gap. This uses the unresolved actual zero displacement and is not a closing estimate.

For an explicitly specified allowed same-q taper, both principal suppliers see every off-line zero. The whole centered correction vector therefore retains rateTheta. A smooth monotone cutoff alone would not guarantee that visibility.

The exact first spectral moments of the literal native inputs have a fixed sum and a one-prime difference. They force BOTH separate squared canonical responses to have rate2Theta. Their signed difference and complete echo still require all covariance, endpoint and normal corrections.
A separate source review confirms the prior actual finite polar-input mismatch. It remains an input restriction, not a response inequality.
